title: mail-parser email header expressions can exhaust parsing workers
summary: Two header-parsing regular expressions have polynomial runtime on attacker-controlled mail. Ordinary parse_from_string, parse_from_bytes and parse_from_file calls can spend excessive CPU on small messages.

severity.rationale: Untrusted mail can keep a parsing worker busy, affecting agent mail ingestion. The vendor documents availability impact without confidentiality or integrity loss, warranting a 30-day response.

exposure: Mail ingestion and analysis processes parsing messages they did not author are exposed. No unusual parsing option or malformed message is required.

remediation.details: Use mail-parser 4.6.1 or later, which replaces the affected parsing logic. If an immediate upgrade is not possible, cap total header size before parsing and enforce a wall-clock timeout around each parse as interim mitigations.
remediation.risk: Updating can interrupt dependent workflows; test compatibility before resuming them.

verification: Confirm the loaded mail-parser package is 4.6.1 or later and test ordinary email parsing.

review.notes: Independent reviewer re-read every tier 1 source and checked every field. No open findings.
